analysis:
The supplied units are base-side excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 4495-5336). The PR changes only documentation: a date bump at line 3, an expanded description of the resource-policy digest at lines 5253-5258 (head side, after the base's line 5253), and a rewritten region at base lines 5374-5376 (head 5379-5389). No code, wire format, key handling, authorization or storage behavior changes in this diff, so no executable security regression is introduced.

The documented change says a build-declared public resident assistant (ClusterPublicModels.tensorAssistant) adds its launch arguments and evidence digest to DistributedInstalledNativeStart.resourcePolicySHA256, so the approval and starts name the declared assistant. That strengthens binding of approvals to the assistant. The doc's claim that the five-field formula is unchanged when no assistant is declared is plausible but unverifiable here. Whether the underlying Swift change in DistributedInstalledNativeStart, NativePairMemberPolicy and the release facts keeps member, owner and coordinator approvals consistent is outside the supplied evidence; the next pass should check it if those source files are in the batch.

The base text pertains to the cluster pair and TP runtime and the pair-serving grants. It touches TB-002 and TB-011 only indirectly. The prose says cluster grants are platform-owned and does not alter the T-041 prefix-cache posture. Cluster prefix scope and tenant partitions are referenced but not changed here. I identified no invalidated threat assumption. The patch excerpt is truncated at the last hunk (head 5379-5389), so the content of that hunk, the rewritten paragraph about the embedded assistant, was not fully visible. That is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.
